scores.why: Ten sheets meet the limit, but sheet 9 has roughly 770 words outside disclosures, and several summaries repeat the evidence immediately below.

fixes.change: Keep the A/B propositions and creative-lead decision visible; move the duplicated blocker list and procedural text into the existing readiness disclosure.
Remove this three-point preview because the numbered decisions immediately repeat it.
Remove the repeated summary bullets; the opening paragraph, evidence tiles and role legend already communicate these points.

scores.why: The essential evidence, deliverables, usage, timing and human responsibilities are covered, but the pilot ask leaves operating-cost estimation and workspace-term confirmation without explicit completion criteria.

fixes.quote: Pilot effort and operating costs are still to be estimated.
fixes.change: Assign management and the operator to estimate setup, training, maintenance and subscription costs in week 1, with sponsor acceptance before retrospective work starts.
Expand the decision to confirm both capacity and the agency workspace’s processing, retention and contractual terms; identify evidence required before client data enters the pilot.

scores.why: The AI/code/people distinction is strong, but unexplained evaluation shorthand and one awkward approval sentence interrupt otherwise accessible language.

fixes.quote: Targets: question precision >80%, draft survival >70%, review <30 minutes; Greek-language quality and voluntary adoption.
fixes.change: Use: 'Targets: leads judge over 80% of questions useful, retain over 70% of draft text, and review each draft in under 30 minutes; also assess Greek quality and voluntary reuse.'

fixes.quote: Signed as the account lead’s was: in the run, by a named person, due before week 4 goes live.
fixes.change: Use: 'Name the creative lead and record their evaluation before week 4; creative remains in shadow mode.'
Use: 'Passing automated checks does not make a brief ready for an account lead to approve.'

scores.why: The answer-first opening and evidence sequence work, but the creative headline softens its own finding and the closing headline promises more than its action list assigns.

fixes.quote: The creative drafts stayed inside the signed-off facts and the spec table, except three things to strike and one call for the creative lead.
fixes.change: Use: 'Creative drafts still need a creative lead: three errors to strike and one claim to judge.'

fixes.quote: Approve the four-week pilot: usage is measured in tokens, the cost of running it is not yet, and week 1 settles both.
fixes.change: Use: 'Approve a conditional four-week pilot, with capacity and operating costs confirmed in week 1.'

scores.why: Brief Builder has a clear name, anatomy, outputs and operating model, but its business benefit and distinctive principles sit behind the implementation story.

fixes.quote: Brief Builder turns a client’s pile of documents into a Greek and English brief.
fixes.change: Add the intended benefit: reducing preparation time and making brief quality more consistent, explicitly presented as pilot goals.

fixes.quote: Ask, don’t guess · Surface, don’t resolve · Flag, don’t correct · Look up, don’t invent · Sign, don’t send
fixes.change: Move this compact principles line out of the ledger and place it directly below the pipeline diagram.

scores.why: The paper, receipt and red-pen system is distinctive and coherent, but the source-defined layout gives long headlines and narrow creative panels excessive visual weight.

fixes.change: Edit takeaway titles to roughly 12–18 words and tune their measure to support two or three lines, preserving more space for evidence.
Compose the square artwork, portrait adaptation and can as one deliberate desktop grouping instead of placing the can alone in a second row; retain a stacked mobile layout.
Move the long technical caption beneath the artwork group so it does not form a narrow column of prose under the portrait image.

scores.why: Headline tokens, model IDs, timings, checks and sign-off match the artifacts, but two provenance descriptions are broader or older than the content they describe.

fixes.quote: Every quote is clipped verbatim from the four source documents
fixes.change: Use: 'Source quotations reproduce the four input documents; output excerpts are identified separately.'

fixes.quote: Clear space of one wordmark height kept free on every side of the name; ring, leaf and name sit in the central column so the 9:16 crop clips nothing
fixes.change: Replace the obsolete ring-and-leaf description with the actual wind stroke and bubbles, and scope any clearance statement to the specific artwork checked.

scores.why: Inline assets, valid local links, keyboard controls and dialog focus handling are sound, but mobile CSS can squeeze Contents and sends important role and correction notes below the main content.

fixes.change: Hide the ten progress ticks below 700px and reserve the middle navigation column for a readable, adequately sized Contents button.
Keep role stamps and essential warnings immediately below the headline; move only supplementary marginal notes after the body.
Retain a visible Next label on phones while hiding only the destination title.

scores.why: The wind-and-fizz identity and can are appealing and honestly labelled, but the can crowds the mandated wordmark clearance and the portrait adaptation knowingly leaves the lockup in the caption zone.

fixes.change: Increase the space above and below the wordmark to at least its height; the inspected can places both the yellow mark and category line too close.

fixes.quote: 9:16 still frame at the TikTok in-feed spec; the lockup sits in TikTok’s caption zone, a dedicated 9:16 layout would raise it
fixes.change: Create that dedicated portrait composition now, raising the lockup and fitting the mock-up label fully within the frame; retain the provisional-spec disclosure.

fixes.quote: Meltemi Fizz is the Greek-made sparkling tea that refreshes your everyday — zero sugar, nothing to feel guilty about.
fixes.change: Keep the recorded draft, but attach the unsupported-origin correction and health-claim review note directly to this proposition so they remain visible beside it on mobile.

overall: Strong evidence-led product story, but not ready to ship unchanged: tighten repetition, simplify mobile navigation and finish the creative adaptations. Hash matched before and after review; no repository files changed. Browser rendering was blocked by the environment, so layout scores rely on HTML/CSS/SVG inspection and direct viewing of the embedded can.
